name: Aptible

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: General Purpose (M) container profile: $0.08/GB RAM-hour, CPU bundled at 1/4 vCPU per GB (4 GB/vCPU), sizes 512MB-240GB, available on Shared & Dedicated stacks, all plans. CPU can burst above allocation when host has spare capacity (not guaranteed). Billed from provisioning; idle containers billed. Per service max 32 containers (dashboard) / 128 (CLI/Terraform).

modes.label: CPU-Optimized (C) container profile
modes.note: Dedicated stacks only; 2GB-368GB; not in every AZ.

plans.name: Development
plans.note: $0 base + usage. Shared stacks only (no dedicated stack, no HIPAA/BAA). General Purpose (M) profile only; no autoscaling.

plans.name: Production
plans.note: $499/month base fee + usage (not a credit). Includes 1 Dedicated Stack; extra Dedicated Stacks $499/stack/month. Unlocks CPU-Optimized/Memory-Optimized profiles, horizontal autoscaling, VPN ($99/peer/mo)/VPC peering, SSO/SAML, HIPAA BAA, HIDS.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom pricing; all Enterprise/volume agreements require a 12-month commitment. Adds self-hosting option (limited release), HITRUST/PCI, vertical autoscaling, 99.95% SLA.

free.note: 30-day free trial of Aptible-hosted resources for business-email sign-ups (existing customers ineligible), no card required; trial scaling limits 3 GB compute, 20 GB storage, 1 endpoint, shared stacks only. No $ credit, so one_time_credit stays null.

caveats: Development $0 platform, Production $499/mo plus resources. Container profiles are priced per GB RAM-hour with CPU bundled: General Purpose (M) $0.08 at 4 GB/vCPU (= $0.32/vCPU-h incl. RAM), CPU-Optimized (C) $0.10 at 2 GB/vCPU ($0.20/vCPU-h), Memory-Optimized (R) $0.05 at 8 GB/vCPU ($0.40/vCPU-h); C and R need Production+. Endpoints $0.06/h, shared HTTP(S) endpoints $0.04/h; dedicated stacks $499/mo, VPN peer $99/mo; databases/backups ($0.02/GB-month) extra. API gateway credits unrelated to compute.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

extras.price: 50% off Production base fee ($250/mo in credits) for first 6 months; <20 engineers, co-marketing required

snapshot_auto.quote: Aptible does not snapshot Persistent Disks.
snapshot_auto.note: App containers have an ephemeral filesystem; restarts/deploys recycle containers. Managed Databases (separate product) get automatic daily backups, not a machine-state snapshot.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Aptible does not take backups of Persistent Disks.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint for app containers or Persistent Disks. Managed Databases support on-demand backups (aptible db:backup) restorable into a new database via backup:restore; not a compute snapshot.

harness_api.quote: Agent harnesses — a dedicated, never-changing base URL per supported coding assistant or agent harness, under /harness/<name>
harness_api.note: Aptible is a Docker-image PaaS (deploy/scale/restart apps and databases); it exposes no API to drive/control an agent harness's execution. The only 'agent harness' surface is the LLM Gateway's per-harness base URL, which just proxies model-inference API calls (OpenAI/Anthropic compatible dialects) for tools like Claude Code — routing, not a harness-control API.

ingress_rules.quote: IP filtering is configured via the Aptible Dashboard on a per-Endpoint basis:
ingress_rules.note: Per-Endpoint IPv4/CIDR allowlists; endpoints are opt-in and can be internal or external; HTTP(S) endpoints support header authentication; apps are unreachable without an Endpoint.

secret_proxy.quote: Aptible's LLM Gateway gives you a single, compliant API for leading model providers, so your team can build securely with AI without having to configure directly with LLM providers.
secret_proxy.note: LLM Gateway (llm-gateway.aptible.com) holds provider access; clients use an Aptible LLM Key (which does enter the app). Separately the MCP Gateway stores upstream MCP-server credentials (shared or per-user; bearer, custom headers, OAuth) so agents call MCP tools without them ('A server holds credentials, exposes a URL, and defines what capabilities are available.' - mcp-gateway/servers): MCP-only, not arbitrary HTTP hosts. Both are standalone gateways, not an in-path proxy for app containers. App secrets are plain environment variables.

volume_attach.quote: A Persistent Disk is a separately-provisioned volume that is mounted into the container and survives the container's lifecycle.
volume_attach.note: AWS EBS gp3, encrypted, resize up; max one disk per Service; Service must be scaled to 1 container; single AZ; no zero-downtime deploys.

volume_shared.quote: the disk cannot be shared across multiple containers
volume_shared.note: A disk can be attached to only one Service at a time, which must run a single container.

isolation.quote: Aptible deploys all resources in Containers. ... Aptible stacks contain several AWS EC2 instances (virtual machines) on which Aptible users deploy their apps and databases in Docker containers.
isolation.note: Shared-kernel Docker containers running on AWS EC2 instances; not per-customer VMs/microVMs.

image_oci.quote: If you need absolute control over your Docker image's build, Aptible lets you deploy directly from a Docker image. ... You push the image to a Docker registry ... You use the aptible deploy command to initiate a deployment on Aptible from the image stored in your registry.
image_oci.note: Deploy any Docker/OCI image from a registry (public or private, incl. AWS ECR).

docker_inside.note: Aptible runs your workload as a shared-kernel Docker container on a multi-tenant/dedicated EC2 host; no docs describe running nested Docker/containers (Docker-in-Docker) inside an App container, and privileged mode is not documented as available.

nested_virt.quote: Aptible deploys all resources in Containers.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Aptible App containers are shared-kernel Docker containers (not VMs); no /dev/kvm or nested virtualization capability is documented.

desktop.quote: Aptible gives your team one place to deploy web apps and databases and govern AI usage, with security & compliance guardrails built-in.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Aptible is a Docker-based PaaS for web apps/databases, not a desktop/VNC product.

browser.quote: Aptible gives your team one place to deploy web apps and databases and govern AI usage, with security & compliance guardrails built-in.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No managed/real browser is provided to running Apps.

computer_use.quote: Aptible gives your team one place to deploy web apps and databases and govern AI usage, with security & compliance guardrails built-in.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No screenshot/click computer-use API exists; Aptible's AI product is the LLM Gateway (model-traffic routing) and MCP Gateway (governing MCP tool access), not a computer-use agent.

anti_bot.quote: Aptible gives your team one place to deploy web apps and databases and govern AI usage, with security & compliance guardrails built-in.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Aptible is a container PaaS, not a browser-automation/scraping product.

captcha_solving.quote: Aptible gives your team one place to deploy web apps and databases and govern AI usage, with security & compliance guardrails built-in.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: Stacks have a single NAT gateway, and all requests originating from an app use the outbound IP addresses associated with that NAT gateway's IP address.
egress_ip_type.note: Outbound IPs come from a pool of AWS datacenter IPs tied to the Stack's NAT gateway, shared across apps on that Stack; not static per-app but a defined pool (card marks static_egress_ip at the stack level).

fork.quote: Aptible gives your team one place to deploy web apps and databases and govern AI usage, with security & compliance guardrails built-in.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No documented feature to clone a running App/container into a new one; scaling launches fresh containers from the same image/config, not a clone of live state.

fork_running.quote: Containers on Aptible are frequently recycled during Operations - meaning new Containers are created during an Operation, and the old ones are terminated.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No live/running clone capability documented.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: By default, the filesystem for your Containers is ephemeral ... Any data stored on the ephemeral filesystem will be gone every time containers are recycled.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No memory/process-state snapshot or fork mechanism exists.

pause_resume.quote: Aptible Apps are scaled at the Service level ... App Services can be scaled by adding more CPU/RAM (vertical scaling) or by adding more containers (horizontal).
pause_resume.note: No documented pause/resume state for App containers; scaling down to 0 containers stops the service but is not framed as a pause/resume-with-reduced-billing feature, and containers billed while running per the card's caveats.

wake_on_request.quote: Containers on Aptible are frequently recycled during Operations
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Aptible has no serverless/sleep-then-wake-on-request behavior; App containers run continuously once scaled up (consistent with card's auto_stop_idle:false).

live_resize.quote: When Apps are scaled, a new set of containers will be launched to replace the existing ones for each of your App's Services.
live_resize.note: Vertical scaling (CPU/RAM) launches new replacement containers rather than resizing a running container in place.

agent_harnesses.quote: Agent harnesses — a dedicated, never-changing base URL per supported coding assistant or agent harness, under /harness/<name>
agent_harnesses.note: The LLM Gateway provides fixed model-inference base URLs for external harnesses (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Grok Build, Pi) to route their LLM API calls through Aptible; it does not preinstall or run a coding-agent harness inside an Aptible sandbox/container.

own_agent_api.quote: Aptible's MCP Gateway gives you control over how your team and AI agents access MCP servers.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Aptible has no first-party browser/computer-use/research task agent; the MCP Gateway and LLM Gateway are governance/routing layers for your own agents/models, not Aptible's own agent.

mcp_server.quote: The gateway sits between your agents and your upstream MCP servers. When an agent makes a tool call, the gateway checks whether that caller is allowed to use that tool, forwards the request if they are, and writes an audit log entry regardless.
mcp_server.note: Aptible's MCP Gateway governs/audits access to third-party upstream MCP servers; it is not an MCP server exposed by Aptible for driving/controlling Aptible Apps/containers.

lang_python.quote: Deploy a Python + Django Template ... Deploy a Python + Flask Demo App
lang_python.note: Any language runs via a Docker image; Aptible also provides first-party Python (Django/Flask) starter templates.

lang_node.note: Any language runs via a Docker image; Aptible also provides a first-party Node.js (Express) starter template.

public_ipv4.quote: These IP addresses are different from the IP addresses associated with an app's Endpoints, which are used for inbound requests.
public_ipv4.note: Inbound traffic reaches Apps via shared/dedicated Endpoints (AWS ELB-backed), not a dedicated public IPv4 assigned directly to each container; outbound IPs come from a shared per-Stack NAT gateway pool.

egress_allowlist.quote: You can share an app's outbound IP address pool with partners or vendors that use an allowlist.
egress_allowlist.note: This feature lets external vendors allowlist Aptible's outbound IPs; it is not a provider-side control letting Aptible customers restrict/allowlist what their own App can reach outbound. No egress allow/deny-list or no-internet mode is documented for App containers.

egress_http_rules.quote: IP filtering is configured via the Aptible Dashboard on a per-Endpoint basis
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. IP filtering and header authentication are inbound (Endpoint) controls; no HTTP method/path-level egress rule engine is documented.

guest_firewall.quote: Aptible deploys all resources in Containers.
guest_firewall.note: Aptible App containers are shared-kernel Docker containers on multi-tenant/dedicated hosts, not a full VM/microVM with guest-controllable root network stack; no docs describe guest-level nftables/iptables control.

gpu.quote: Aptible offers three Container Profiles with unique CPU-to-RAM ratios and sizes: General Purpose (M) ... CPU-Optimized (C) ... Memory Optimized (R)
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Only CPU/RAM container profiles are documented; no GPU instance type is offered.

open_source.quote: Aptible gives your team one place to deploy web apps and databases and govern AI usage, with security & compliance guardrails built-in.
open_source.note: Aptible is a commercial managed PaaS; no evidence the core platform is released under an OSI license (the Aptible CLI is a client tool, not the core service).

max_session_h.quote: Containers on Aptible are frequently recycled during Operations - meaning new Containers are created during an Operation, and the old ones are terminated.
max_session_h.note: Apps run continuously until redeployed/restarted/scaled/stopped by the user; there is no maximum single-session runtime limit imposed by Aptible.

snapshot.quote: Automatic backups. Aptible does not snapshot Persistent Disks. Backing up disk contents is your responsibility.
snapshot.note: App containers run an ephemeral filesystem; the attached Persistent Disk (AWS EBS gp3) has no first-party snapshot/backup mechanism ('Aptible does not take backups of Persistent Disks... Persistent Disks have no automatic backup system'). Only separate Managed Databases get automatic daily backups, which is a different product, not a compute/VM snapshot.

auto_stop_idle.quote: When Horizontal Autoscaling is enabled on a Service, the autoscaler evaluates Services every 5 minutes and generates scaling adjusted based on CPU usage (as percentage of total cores).
auto_stop_idle.note: Autoscaling (horizontal/vertical) reacts to CPU/RAM usage, not idleness, and never scales below the configured Minimum Container Count (no scale-to-zero). Container docs describe containers persisting continuously and only recycling on deploy/restart/scale, with no idle-timeout stop. Pricing/caveats also state idle containers are billed. No idle-based auto-stop feature is documented.

windows.quote: On Aptible, a Docker image is used to deploy app containers.
windows.note: Aptible deploys Linux Docker containers on AWS-backed Shared/Dedicated Stacks; no Windows container/OS option is documented anywhere in the docs, pricing, or container-profile pages. Outside the product's scope.

macos.quote: On Aptible, a Docker image is used to deploy app containers.
macos.note: Same Linux-Docker-container PaaS model; no macOS runtime is offered or mentioned anywhere in the docs/pricing. Outside the product's scope.

arm64.quote: Aptible stacks contain several AWS EC2 instances (virtual machines) on which Aptible users deploy their apps and databases in Docker containers.
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Aptible's docs (architecture, container profiles, image/Dockerfile deploy guides) describe only its three x86-oriented Container Profiles on AWS EC2 hosts; no ARM/Graviton/aarch64 instance option, image architecture choice, or multi-arch build guidance is documented anywhere in the docs, pricing, or container-profile pages.

cpu_class.quote: Scaling up resources in Aptible directly increases the guaranteed CPU Allocation for a container. However, containers can sometimes burst above their CPU allocation if the underlying infrastructure host has available capacity. ... if a container is scaled to a 4GB general-purpose container, it would have a 1 vCPU allocation or 100% CPU utilization in our metrics.
cpu_class.note: Applies uniformly to all Container Profiles (General Purpose/M, CPU-Optimized/C, Memory Optimized/R): each container gets a guaranteed CPU allocation proportional to its size (100% of its allocated vCPU is the guaranteed baseline), and can opportunistically burst above that (observed >100%, e.g. 150%+) only when the shared host has spare capacity, which is not guaranteed -- the classic burstable pattern with a 100% published baseline per allocated vCPU, not dedicated/reserved cores and not plain oversubscribed sharing with no guarantee.
